mechanism: The code reading is exact and the consequence is worse than the finding states. COMPUTE-INPUT-SIGNATURES (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:407) dispatches on the solver's script-type-name string; its cond covers "pubkeyhash" (:487), "witness_v0_keyhash" (:493), "witness_v1_taproot" (:503), "scripthash" (:535), "witness_v0_scripthash" (:577) and bare multisig (:595), then falls through at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:599 to (fail "unsupported scriptPubKey type ~A"). Core's SignStep answers TxoutType::PUBKEY as its FIRST case (refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:643-647): CreateSig over vSolutions[0] and push the signature -- no pubkey is pushed, the scriptPubKey already carries it. This one function is the node's ONLY per-input signer: SIGN-TX-INPUTS calls it at rawtransaction.lisp:727 and is driven by signrawtransactionwithkey (:831) and by %WALLET-SIGN-TRANSACTION (src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:1853-1860), which is what %FINISH-TRANSACTION (send/sendtoaddress/sendall, wallet-spend.lisp:3042), the fund path (:2326, :3673) and signrawtransactionwithwallet run; the PSBT signer calls it directly (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:1321) for walletprocesspsbt and descriptorprocesspsbt. So there is no second signer to fall back on. On the ownership side the coin is fully adopted: the combo() expansion emits the bare-P2PK script (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:1495-1500, Core's legacy-migration shape), and %SCRIPT-SAT-WEIGHT sizes a :PUBKEY input at src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:505, so the coin is marked solvable and spendable and coin selection may pick it. Refuter checks that FAILED to refute it: (1) coin selection does NOT exclude the coin -- listunspent reports spendable=true, solvable=true and getbalances counts it as trusted; (2) the PSBT escape does not exist -- walletprocesspsbt and descriptorprocesspsbt (handed the exact combo() descriptor including the WIF) both return complete=false and write no partial signature; (3) it is not a wallet-only gap -- signrawtransactionwithkey handed the exact WIF refuses too, while the P2PKH of the SAME key signs.
consequence: S1: funds the wallet owns, reports spendable and selects cannot be spent by ANY path in the node. Executed end to end on regtest with a wallet whose ONLY coin was a bare-P2PK output of an imported combo() descriptor: getbalances trusted 49.999; sendtoaddress raised RPC -6 "Signing transaction failed" (a hard error, no partial result); sendall returned complete=false plus an unfinalizable PSBT and broadcast nothing; signrawtransactionwithwallet returned complete=false with "unsupported scriptPubKey type pubkey"; walletprocesspsbt returned complete=false having added only a BIP32 derivation record; descriptorprocesspsbt with the combo() descriptor carrying the private key returned complete=false and added nothing. With a second, P2PKH coin present the damage spreads: sendall selected BOTH coins, signed only the P2PKH input and returned complete=false, so the presence of one P2PK coin blocks the sweep of the rest of the wallet. combo() is the descriptor Core's own legacy-wallet migration emits and the shape used to recover a pre-2012 P2PK key, so this is the funds-recovery path, not an exotic corner. Honest bound: the money is stuck in OUR node, not destroyed -- listdescriptors true still exports the WIF, so another implementation can sign it; and a user who never imports combo()/pk() and is never paid to a bare-P2PK output never meets it. Both bounds are outside the wallet's own flow, which is the S1 bar.

fix_shape: Add the missing arm to COMPUTE-INPUT-SIGNATURES, mirroring Core's SignStep TxoutType::PUBKEY (sign.cpp:643-647) and the existing :P2PKH arm. In the cond at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:486, before the bare-multisig clause, match (string= type "pubkey"): take the pubkey the solver already extracted (bl.val:classify-script's :pubkeys / the push payload of the scriptPubKey rather than re-parsing the script), look it up in PUBMAP -- which is keyed by full pubkey and is what the multisig arms already use, so an uncompressed 65-byte key works too -- fail with the existing "no key for P2PK" wording when it is absent, and otherwise build an input-sig of a new kind :P2PK with :needed 1 and one ECDSA pair whose sighash is the LEGACY one over the whole scriptPubKey ((legacy-sig spk key), exactly as :P2PKH does). Then add the matching arm to %FINALIZE-INPUT-SIGNATURES (rawtransaction.lisp:604): the scriptSig is the signature push ALONE -- (bl.ser:script-push-data sig) with no pubkey after it -- and no witness. Because %FINALIZE-INPUT-SIGNATURES is an ECASE, forgetting the second half is a loud error rather than a silent miss. Nothing in %WALLET-SIGN-MAPS needs changing: the combo() SPKM already registers the key in PUBMAP, which is why the P2PKH sibling signs today. Cover it with a regtest test that imports combo(WIF), funds the bare-P2PK script only, and asserts sendall broadcasts a complete transaction that passes %VERIFY-TX-SCRIPTS, plus a signrawtransactionwithkey unit case with the P2PKH control alongside so a future regression cannot pass vacuously.
